title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Possible inconsistency in (75ter): relation (75) of the previous page, λ_0 = g_0 h_0^{-γ} λ, with g_0 = h_0 = 1 would force λ_0 = λ. The bracketed values λ_0 = τ_∞, λ = l_0^{-1}τ_∞ differ by l_0^{-1}. Either (75) involves a twist when p = −1 (elements outside π̂_{0,3}, in Ĝ^*), or the bracketed line is provisional. Grothendieck flags it with 'cf. ci-dessous'.

ideas.what: Multiplier-1 locus characterised by the 2-cycle relation σ_∞(ξ) = ξ^{-1} and the 3-cycle relation hρ(h)ρ²(h) = 1, i.e. Drinfeld's relations with m = 0, together with γ = (p−1)/2.
ideas.modern_name: Defining relations (I), (II) of GT^ restricted to λ = 1; kernel of the cyclotomic character on GT^
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only announces the program of describing Γ_Q via its action on the Teichmüller tower, without these equations.

ideas.what: Complex conjugation as explicit element with multiplier −1 and trivial 'f' (g_0 = h_0 = 1).
Desire for explicit elements of the combinatorially defined group to test whether the necessary conditions from Γ_Q are automatically satisfied.
ideas.modern_name: Ihara's question whether Γ_Q → GT^ is an isomorphism; scarcity of explicit GT^ elements

deep.surprise_reason: The page independently arrives (pre-Drinfeld, presumably) at the GT relations in the λ = 1 case and at complex conjugation as (−1, 1). This is historically nice evidence of Grothendieck anticipating GT, already documented in discussions of the Longue Marche, but it contains no result absent from the later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Aut_loc' is more likely 'Aut_lac' (loop-preserving, cf. Autext_{ℓc} on the previous page).
Condition (iv) reads h_0 = ξ (same symbol ξ as in (v)).
The margin note at the end of (75ter) reads roughly '← cf. ci-dessous' followed by a partially legible phrase.
In (75ter), λ' line: '[-λ'=-] g_0^{-1}λ_0 = l_0^{-1}' with crossed-out exponents.
